doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Why he left Dizzy after eight years
summary: Playing the same set every night had grown stale, though leaving Dizzy was hard; Baker raises Las Vegas and they take a break.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Then after those 8 years with Dizzy, did you leave for a specific reason to do something else at that time?
Well, I guess, it was -- I guess -- I guess, yeah, because I just wanted to, I guess, maybe do something else. You know.
So you were playing pretty much the same repertoire -­
Yeah. Uh-huh. [affirmative]
-- across that time -­
Uh-huh. [affirmative]
-- with the same people, and knowing you and your desire -­
Yes.
-- to always feel like you need to grow -­
Well.
-- was that a difficult situation to do pretty much the same thing for 8 years?
It was. In a way, it was because every night at 10:00, I'd know exactly what we'd be playing, you know, [indiscernible] so -- so. I, you know, and then I just, you know.
Uh-huh. [affirmative] And it must be hard because you -- you loved Dizzy so much -­
Yeah!
-- that to go and do something else -­
Yeah.
-- that must've been difficult for you.
Yeah. So -- so I left and then we had -- what did I get after that?
Was that when you went to Vegas or?
I think after that, I did.
Because -­
I did.
-- that's not a musical scene that's well-known or well-documented. I really wanted to ask you some things about, you know -­
'Bout Vegas?
About Vegas and what was happening in the whole scene out there. Especially for black musicians at that time.
Yeah. Could we -- could we -- ?
Take a break?
For a minute? Yeah.
Sure.
I just wanna open that window.
